report.summary: The section is aspirational and unenforceable; no rule is stated that can be mechanically checked, so an agent can claim compliance while ignoring the intent.
risks: 11.1 | high | 'wire it through the canonical kernel or keep it as a disposable, isolated experiment' is a policy with no definition of 'canonical kernel' or 'isolated experiment', so an agent can claim any code path satisfies it. | Define 'canonical kernel' and 'isolated experiment' with explicit criteria; show a commit that violates the rule but passes a keyword check.

11.2 | medium | 'The next product proof is the Gate 1 ignition slice, not a broader assistant demo' is a prioritization statement with no binding mechanism; an engineer can still build a broader demo and claim it is preparation for the ignition slice. | Add a gate in the CI pipeline that rejects any commit that adds a feature not on the Gate 1 roadmap.
todos: Replace the paragraph with a machine-enforceable rule, e.g., 'All new feature work must be gated behind a feature flag that is disabled by default and requires explicit approval from the kernel maintainer to enable.'
Define 'canonical kernel' and 'isolated experiment' with measurable criteria in a glossary.
Add a requirement that any new feature not on the Gate 1 path must be accompanied by an experiment tag and a removal date.

claims.claim: Until Gate 0 exits, the default answer to new feature work is: wire it through the canonical kernel or keep it as a disposable, isolated experiment.
claims.why: The rule is a policy directive but lacks operational definitions. 'Canonical kernel' and 'disposable, isolated experiment' are undefined. An agent can claim any code path satisfies 'wire it through the canonical kernel' because there is no specification of what that means. Similarly, 'isolated experiment' has no criteria for isolation or disposability. The rule is unenforceable as written.

claims.claim: The next product proof is the Gate 1 ignition slice, not a broader assistant demo.
claims.why: This is a statement of priority, not a rule. It does not forbid building a broader assistant demo; it only says that the next proof is the ignition slice. A careless engineer can comply formally by saying they are building toward the ignition slice while actually building a broader demo. No mechanism is provided to enforce this priority.
